preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 2 and 58 inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 blue and n-1 red arc definitions provided.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= b <= n and 1 <= r <= n for b, r in zip(blue_arcs, red_arcs))
preconditions.description: All arc destinations are valid vertex indices between 1 and n.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 5000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v < n and len(s) == n - 1 and all(c in 'RB' for c in s) for v, s in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query specifies a valid vertex v (1 to n-1) and a string s of length n-1 containing only 'R' and 'B'.
It is guaranteed that vertex n is reachable from every vertex in the graph.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all((int(line) == -1) or (int(line) >= 0) for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either -1 (unreachable) or a non-negative integer representing time.

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) == -1) == (not is_reachable(queries[i], n, blue_arcs, red_arcs)) for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: For each query i, the output is -1 if and only if the state (v, s) is unreachable from the initial state.

postconditions.expression: all((int(output_lines[i]) == -1) or (int(output_lines[i]) == first_time(queries[i], n, blue_arcs, red_arcs)) for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: For each reachable query i, the output is the smallest non-negative integer t such that the state (v, s) appears at time t.
